# Verdict page states the success criteria

- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; one line)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Product direction (purpose level), 2026-10-28 (VISION ruling 7: Phrase is not meant to beat C#; it solves the problems of AI-written code being unaccountable, unverifiable at the speed it is written, with intent vanishing with the prompt) and Decider D99 (Codex Yes, Grok Support-it). The head-to-head benchmark stays published as context and is not the success measure.
- **Depends on:** 138
- **Story:** As the product owner, I want the verdict page to say what Phrase's success criteria are, so that nobody reads the head-to-head numbers as the success measure.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given scripts/verdict.py, When the page is generated, Then it states in one line, quoting VISION ruling 7, that Phrase's success criteria are verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability and not out-performing C# on raw token cost, directly under the headline and before the vocabulary-pause sentence, and a test fails if the line is missing
  2. Given the headline and the frozen D32 numbers, When the page is generated, Then they are unchanged (no score is altered, the benchmark is still published honestly)
  3. Given the published page docs/results/verdict-DATE.md, When it is regenerated, Then it carries the line and the repository checks stay green

## Context

- Ruling 7 text is in VISION.md. A card, not a direct edit, because verdict.py is code with tests.
